newsitem.title: USA: CBOT okays increased role in Clearing Corporation.
newsitem.headline: CBOT okays increased role in Clearing Corporation.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) directors approved a plan to designate two CBOT directors to the board of governors at the Board of Trade Clearing Corporation (BOTCC), the CBOT's independent clearinghouse, the exchange said.

The BOTCC earlier endorsed the CBOT's intention to increase the exchange's representation at the clearinghouse, but BOTCC governors and the BOTCC's roughly 130 shareholders still must formally approve the plan.
"I view it as a shareholder issue," John Hiatt, BOTCC president said in an interview. "It's their issue."
BOTCC shareholders are clearing members of the CBOT.
Under the proposal, two CBOT directors will serve staggered two-year terms as BOTCC governors. Each year, a CBOT director will be selected by a majority of the CBOT board.
The CBOT hopes to designate a CBOT director for a two-year term by the beginning of 1997, a CBOT spokesman said.
In 1998, a second CBOT director will be chosen to serve a two-year term as a BOTCC governor. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
